one_sentence: Theophysics argues that every physical law has a structurally identical spiritual counterpart, differing only by a free-will term, and that full integration yields mathematical identity between physical and spiritual coherence.
executive_summary: This document presents the complete framework of Theophysics, claiming that the mathematical structure of physical laws—from gravity to quantum mechanics—maps exactly onto spiritual realities such as love, sin, faith, and grace. Each of the ten laws is paired with a spiritual analog that differs by exactly one asymmetry term representing free will. The framework culminates in a master equation where total physical coherence equals total spiritual coherence, and a self-recursive dynamic system whose equilibrium condition mathematically describes salvation. The document also includes an unprovability theorem arguing that the ground of all systems must be non-physical, necessary, non-formal, and self-grounding—the classical definition of God. The conclusion is that mathematics requires an external, infinite source of grace for any system to maintain coherence indefinitely.
short_summary: This document is the canonical explanation of the Theophysics framework, presenting ten laws that pair physical equations with spiritual counterparts. The core structural claim is that every physical law has an identical spiritual analog differing only by a free-will asymmetry term. Key evidence includes the exact mathematical match between Shannon entropy and the Logos information equation, and the QCD potential matching the love binding equation. This matters because it provides a formal mathematical argument that faith and reason are not in conflict, and that the properties of the required external ground match the classical definition of God.
